study_identification_part.si4_title: Beyond homogeneity: charting the landscape of heterogeneity in neurodevelopmental and psychiatric electroencephalography

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To combine high-density EEG with normative modeling to quantify electrophysiological heterogeneity in spectral power and functional connectivity among patients with neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders (ADHD, ASD, anxiety, learning disorder), and to explore whether deviation-based markers can enhance comparative analysis and correlate with clinical assessments.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The normative models were trained on 448 healthy controls; an additional 112 healthy subjects were held out as an independent comparison set.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: "Models were trained on 448 (52% M) healthy controls (HC) and 112 (55% M) healthy subjects were held out as a comparison group..."

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: The imaging modality is clearly described as high-density EEG (HD-EEG) with 128 channels. Resting-state paradigm with eyes open is noted. EEG was acquired using Geodesic HydroCel systems across all datasets.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: Resting-state HD-EEG (128 channels) data was collected from subjects aged between 5 and 18 years old across multiple datasets. ... High-density EEG data was recorded in an acoustically isolated room using a 128-channel EEG Geodesic HydroCel system provided by Electrical Geodesics Inc. (EGI) during a resting-state paradigm, where participants were instructed to fixate on a cross displayed at the center of a computer screen and to open or close their eyes at different time points.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Deviation patterns are highly heterogeneous and frequency-dependent with low spatial overlap; deviation-based analyses enhance group differentiation; global deviation correlates with clinical assessment (ADOS).
